text: {"question":"How does the updated determination of the Hubble constant from the later study differ from the earlier value reported when combining CMB, BAO, and supernova data?","reference_answer":"The earlier analysis found H0 ≈ 73.26 ± 0.98 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, whereas the later study, after correcting the Pantheon+ magnitudes and incorporating DES‑DOVEKIE data, reports H0 ≈ 73.26 ± 0.81 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹—essentially the same central value but with a slightly reduced uncertainty and a more precise assessment of the tension with the CMB‑ΛCDM result."}
